summary: Sumac, a 100-foot Forest Service stair tower in Cass County, was probably erected in the 1930s and was sold and removed in the 1972 Chippewa National Forest tower sale.

facts.status_note: Sold and removed in 1972; no source read says what, if anything, remains at the site
facts.agency: US Forest Service, Chippewa National Forest

events.note: Towerman's residence at Sumac Hill completed in June 1939, per Forest Lookouts; the residence, not the tower
Sold and removed in the 1972 Chippewa National Forest tower sale

evidence.supports: 100-foot stair tower owned by the US Forest Service (USFS)

evidence.quote: Sumac was probably erected in the 1930s.

evidence.supports: sold and removed in the 1972 Chippewa National Forest tower sale
evidence.quote: It was sold and ... in the 1972 Chippewa National Forest tower sale.

evidence.supports: Sumac Hill lookout in the Chippewa National Forest; towerman's residence completed June 1939
evidence.quote: Chippewa National Forest June 1939: The towerman's residence was completed.

evidence.supports: FFLA list shows Sumac in Cass County as Tower Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Cass County list calls it the Sumac Fire Tower and Forest Lookouts calls it Sumac Hill in the Chippewa National Forest; both fit the record's Sumac in Cass County. Treated as one tower on name and county alone.

sources.title: Cass County Minnesota Fire Lookout Towers (PDF)

notes_for_editor: Identity is matched by name and county only: the Cass list says Sumac Fire Tower, the Forest Lookouts page says Sumac Hill; the record's coordinates do not appear on the Cass list. No built year is given beyond probably the 1930s, so no built event. The 1939 event is the towerman's residence, not the tower. No source found describes what remains at the site. The unsourced visit.climbable flag was removed from facts on the fact-check pass. A Chippewa National Forest tower-loop guide (thedirtymule.com) returned HTTP 403 and was not read. Used 1 WebSearch call and about 3 page reads.
